answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Fast verification algorithms like falcon authenticate hardware roots, while a lantern protocol tracks stake across clusters. Generating identity proofs requires solving verifiable puzzles whose stake requirement scales exponentially with node count, forcing exponential capital exhaustion for Sybil swarms. A verification sonnet commits cluster metrics on-chain, ensuring superlinear attacker cost.
